EC1: 1. Expected performance of PCI < 60 minutes from diagnosis (qualifying ECG) or inability to arrive at the catheterisation laboratory within 3 hours
EC3: Left bundle branch block [OR] or ventricular pacing
EC4: Patients with cardiogenic shock [AND] - Killip Class 4
EC5: Patients with a body weight < 55 kg (known or estimated)
EC6: Uncontrolled hypertension [AND], defined as sustained blood pressure = 180/110 mm Hg (systolic BP [OR] = 180 mm Hg and/or diastolic BP = 110 mm Hg) prior to randomisation
EC8: Recent administration of any i.v. or s.c. anticoagulation within 12 hours, including unfractionated heparin [OR], enoxaparin [OR], and/or bivalirudin [OR] or current use of oral anticoagulation (i.e. warfarin [OR] or a NOACs)
EC9: Active bleeding [OR] or known bleeding disorder [OR]/diathesis
EC10: Known history of central nervous system damage (i.e. neoplasm [OR], aneurysm [OR], intracranial [OR] or spinal surgery) or recent trauma to the head [OR] or cranium (i.e. < 3 months)
EC11: Major surgery [OR], biopsy [OR] of a parenchymal organ, or significant trauma within the past 2 months (this includes any trauma associated with the current myocardial infarction)
EC12: Clinical diagnosis associated with increased risk of bleeding including known active peptic ulceration [OR] and/or neoplasm with increased bleeding risk
EC13: Prolonged cardiopulmonary resuscitation (> 2 minutes) within the past 2 weeks
EC14: Known acute pericarditis [OR] and/or subacute bacterial endocarditis
EC15: Known acute pancreatitis [OR] or known severe hepatic dysfunction, including hepatic failure [OR], cirrhosis [OR], portal hypertension [OR] (oesophageal varices) and active hepatitis
EC18: Previous enrolment in this study or treatment with an investigational drug or device under another study protocol in the past 7 days
EC19: Known allergic reactions to tenecteplase [OR], clopidogrel [OR], enoxaparin [OR] and aspirin
EC20: Inability to follow the protocol and comply with follow-up requirements or any other reason that the investigator feels would place the patient at increased risk if the investigational therapy is initiated.
